newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: NATO wants Russia talks on target by July summit.
newsitem.headline: NATO wants Russia talks on target by July summit.

text.p: NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana said on Thursday he wanted to have negotiations on bilateral relations with Russia "on target" by the time of the Atlantic alliance's summit in Madrid in July.
"We don't know when we will be able to finish this exercise but we are going to start soon. We hope to have it on target by the time of the summit," Solana told reporters on a visit to Vienna.
"We are prepared to go as far as possible in order to get good, solid, long-lasting bilateral relations with Russia," Solana said.
"We do think...bilateral relations with Russia are important for everybody, it is important for the security of our continent of Europe."
The July summit of the 16-member alliance is expected to decide on which former Soviet bloc countries would be invited to into an expanded NATO, a move which Moscow has so far opposed.

Solana, a former Spanish foreign minister, declined to elaborate on reports that NATO was planning a package of sweeteners, including economic assistance and arms control changes. But he said a modernisation of the Conventional Forces in Europe (CFE) treaty -- a longstanding Russian wish -- would be important.
